clips.speaker: Olivia Solon
clips.title: 彭博社Olivia Solon：揭秘“Cookie填充”如何窃取电商佣金

subtitles.en: To break this all down, Bloomberg News looked into it and technology editor Olivia Solon joins us now.
subtitles.zh: 彭博新闻对此进行了调查，科技编辑Olivia Solon现在加入我们。

subtitles.en: This is complicated to explain. I think I understand it, but I think you will explain it better.
subtitles.zh: 这解释起来有点复杂。我觉得我懂了，但你能说得更清楚。

subtitles.en: So please explain to us what cookie-stuffing is and why it matters and why it's considered fraud, essentially.
subtitles.zh: 请解释什么是Cookie填充，为什么它重要，以及为什么它被视为欺诈。

subtitles.en: Well, buckle up for a little explainer of affiliate marketing first. At its most basic, this is where retailers will pay a small commission to either publishers or influencers who send someone to buy something on their website.
subtitles.zh: 先来简单解释一下联盟营销。最基本的是，零售商向将用户引导至其网站并促成购买的发布商或网红支付小额佣金。

subtitles.en: So let's say you're on a review site like Wirecutter and you're looking for laptops, you decide to buy one, you click through from Wirecutter to Walmart. And the link that you use to land on Walmart's page will have a special code in it, which will result in a little web cookie, there's the cookie, being left on the person's browser that basically says this shop came from Wirecutter.
subtitles.zh: 假设你在Wirecutter这样的评测网站上看笔记本电脑，决定购买，从Wirecutter点击进入沃尔玛。链接中带有特殊代码，会在浏览器中留下一个小型网络Cookie，表明这次访问来自Wirecutter。

subtitles.en: So when that person buys the laptop, Walmart pays a commission to Wirecutter. But the key thing is to get the commission, the user has to have intentionally interacted with the affiliate in this case, Wirecutter.
subtitles.zh: 当用户购买笔记本电脑时，沃尔玛向Wirecutter支付佣金。但关键是，要获得佣金，用户必须有意与联盟伙伴（此处为Wirecutter）互动。

subtitles.en: So clicking through from Wirecutter to Walmart. Now, fear is a startup. It has an app which lets you browse for close. And it also has this browser extension, which is a little program that you add to your browser.
subtitles.zh: 即从Wirecutter点击进入沃尔玛。Fear是一家初创公司，它有一个应用可以让你浏览商品，还有一个浏览器扩展程序。

clips.speaker: Olivia Solon
clips.title: 彭博社Olivia Solon：Fear扩展在后台自动点击，劫持佣金

subtitles.en: And as you're looking on e-commerce sites, it kind of offers you discount codes. And in theory, fear should only get the commission if a shopper clicks on one of those discount codes or clicks through from the fear app to buying something.
subtitles.zh: 当你在电商网站浏览时，它会提供折扣码。理论上，Fear只有在用户点击折扣码或从Fear应用点击购买时才能获得佣金。

subtitles.en: That's all like very normal way of affiliate marketing working. But what we found was that if you had the fear extension installed on your mobile browser, it would fire an automatic click in the background.
subtitles.zh: 这完全是联盟营销的正常方式。但我们发现，如果你在移动浏览器上安装了Fear扩展，它会在后台自动触发一次点击。

subtitles.en: The moment you put something in your shopping cart on any of the sites that had partner with, even if you didn't interact with fears app or extension.
subtitles.zh: 当你在任何合作网站上将商品加入购物车时，即使你没有与Fear的应用或扩展互动。

subtitles.en: So to go back to the Wirecutter example, you'd click through from Wirecutter, put the laptop in your shopping cart, and fear would automatically click in the background, open a new tab that the user wouldn't see because you're on your mobile browser and you just see the one you're on.
subtitles.zh: 回到Wirecutter的例子，你从Wirecutter点击进入，将笔记本电脑加入购物车，Fear会在后台自动点击，打开一个新标签页，用户看不到，因为移动浏览器上只显示当前页面。

subtitles.en: And in doing so, set the fear cookie overriding the Wirecutter cookie. And that allows it to take the credit for the subsequent sale, which it's not supposed to do. So instead of Wirecutter getting the commission fear would, it would also do something similar if you just go straight to a retailer's website with no referral from another website.
subtitles.zh: 这样，Fear的Cookie覆盖了Wirecutter的Cookie，从而窃取了后续销售的功劳。Wirecutter拿不到佣金，Fear却拿到了。如果你直接访问零售商网站，没有其他网站推荐，它也会做类似的事。

clips.speaker: Olivia Solon
clips.title: 彭博社Olivia Solon：Fear扩展行为涉嫌欺诈，违反服务条款

subtitles.en: So it was kind of getting a commission for a sale that would have happened anyway. And we tested this across more than 50 retailers websites and found it was consistently happening over our testing period of, it was a little over a week long.
subtitles.zh: 它实际上是在为本来就会发生的销售获取佣金。我们在超过50家零售商网站上进行了测试，发现这种情况在整个测试期间（一周多一点）持续发生。

subtitles.en: Olivia, this Christina used the word fraud a moment ago. This has a whiff of fraud to it. It does seem like it's in violation of terms of service.
subtitles.zh: Olivia，Christina刚才用了“欺诈”这个词。这确实有欺诈的味道，似乎违反了服务条款。

subtitles.en: When you look at the potential illegality of this, what do we find here? Were they kind of circumventing rules, doing something kind of an enterprising practice to be most charitable sort of? Where does this fall in the spectrum of online fraud?
subtitles.zh: 从潜在违法性来看，我们发现了什么？他们是在规避规则，还是说好听点是一种进取的做法？这在网络欺诈中属于什么程度？
